name: Darifenacin pivotal trial
question: Does once-daily darifenacin reduce overactive bladder symptoms more than placebo?

design.population: 561 patients aged 19–88 years (85% female) with overactive bladder symptoms for more than 6 months, including 5–50 urge-incontinence episodes per week, at least 8 voids per day, and urgency at least once per day; some had used antimuscarinics and previous nonresponse was allowed.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 421–422; Table 1, p 423

verdictNote: Both prespecified dose comparisons met the primary endpoint; 3.75 mg was not formally tested.
takeaway: In a 12-week randomized trial of 561 patients with overactive bladder, once-daily darifenacin 7.5 mg and 15 mg reduced median weekly incontinence episodes more than placebo (treatment differences −1.5 and −2.1 episodes/week); 3.75 mg was not formally tested.

reports.label: 12-week primary report
reports.citation: Haab F, Stewart L, Dwyer P. Darifenacin, an M3 selective receptor antagonist, is an effective and well-tolerated once-daily treatment for overactive bladder. *Eur Urol.* 2004;45(4):420-429. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2004.01.008

results.measure: Full-analysis-set median change in incontinence episodes/week from baseline to week 12, darifenacin 7.5 mg versus placebo
results.note: Median treatment difference in episodes/week versus placebo; the full analysis set required randomization, at least one dose, and baseline plus post-baseline efficacy data. Endpoint-specific analysis denominators were not reported. The 15 mg comparison preceded 7.5 mg testing at two-sided alpha 0.05.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 422–423; Table 2, p 424

results.measure: Full-analysis-set median change in incontinence episodes/week from baseline to week 12, darifenacin 15 mg versus placebo
results.note: Median treatment difference in episodes/week versus placebo; 15 mg was tested first at two-sided alpha 0.05. The 3.75 mg null-dose arm had no formal sample sizing or statistical test.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 422–423; Table 2, p 424

results.measure: Full-analysis-set median change in micturitions/day from baseline to week 12
results.note: Median treatment difference versus placebo: 7.5 mg −0.8/day (95% CI −1.2 to −0.4), P<0.001; 15 mg −0.9/day (95% CI −1.4 to −0.4), P<0.001.

results.measure: Full-analysis-set median change in urgency episodes/day and 0–100 mm urgency severity scale from baseline to week 12
results.note: Frequency median treatment differences versus placebo: 7.5 mg −0.9/day (95% CI −1.5 to −0.4), P=0.001; 15 mg −0.9/day (95% CI −1.5 to −0.3), P=0.005. Severity median differences: 7.5 mg −4.7 mm (95% CI −8.0 to −1.9), P=0.001; 15 mg −5.2 mm (95% CI −8.6 to −1.9), P=0.002.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 422; Table 3, p 425

results.measure: Full-analysis-set median change in volume voided per micturition from baseline to week 12
results.note: Median treatment difference versus placebo: 7.5 mg +9.1 mL (95% CI +0.4 to +17.8), P=0.040; 15 mg +20.7 mL (95% CI +9.6 to +32.6), P<0.001.

results.endpoint: Incontinence requiring pad or clothing change
results.measure: Full-analysis-set median change in episodes/week from baseline to week 12
results.note: Median treatment difference versus placebo: 7.5 mg −1.3/week (95% CI −2.0 to −0.5), P<0.001; 15 mg −1.3/week (95% CI −2.3 to −0.3), P=0.002.

results.measure: Full-analysis-set median change in nocturnal awakenings/week from baseline to week 12, darifenacin 15 mg versus placebo
results.note: The prespecified 15 mg comparison was nonsignificant; 7.5 mg was therefore not formally tested under the dose-testing sequence.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis, p 422; Table 3, p 425

harms.label: Constipation-related and other treatment-related discontinuation
harms.locator: Full text, Table 4 and footnotes, p 426
harms.note: No patient withdrew because of dry mouth. Treatment-related discontinuations also included rash (7.5 mg), urticaria with tongue edema and flatulence with insomnia (15 mg), and voiding difficulty (placebo).

harms.label: Treatment-related dry mouth and constipation
harms.locator: Full text, Adverse events, pp 424–426; Table 4, p 426
harms.note: Table 4 gives investigator-attributed treatment-related events; 84% of patients reporting adverse events had only mild or moderate events. No blurred vision was reported; CNS and cardiac safety profiles were described as comparable to placebo.

harms.label: Serious adverse events, all causality
harms.note: Eight serious AEs overall; a second-degree atrioventricular block in the 7.5 mg arm was deemed unlikely caused by study drug after review of prior history.

delivery.label: Treatment and diary schedule
delivery.value: Controlled-release darifenacin 3.75, 7.5 or 15 mg or matching placebo was taken orally once daily for 12 weeks after medication washout and a 2-week placebo run-in; electronic diaries preceded visits at weeks 2, 6 and 12. Of 561 randomized and treated, 526 completed treatment: 49/53, 219/229, 106/115 and 152/164 in the 3.75 mg, 7.5 mg, 15 mg and placebo arms. Compliance exceeded 86% in all but two patients; 462/561 (82.4%) had 100% compliance by tablet count.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 421–423
